sections.title: How LLMs behave

blocks.title: Not from your PDFs
blocks.text: No guide of yours covers this, so this page was written for the site, as of October 2026. Tools and versions change quickly: check the official documentation before relying on details.

blocks: You can treat an LLM as an unusual remote service: stateless, slow, priced per use, and non-deterministic. Those properties drive all of the engineering.

rows: A chunk of text; the unit of billing and limits
Count them; long prompts cost more
The most tokens a model can consider in one request
Select what you send; you cannot send everything
The model remembers nothing between calls
You resend history: chat memory is your job
Low for extraction; higher for creative text
Ground answers in data; verify; never trust blindly
Parse into a Java record, and validate
The model asks your code to run a function
Your code runs it, and is the security boundary

sequenceDiagram
  participant U as User

  U->>A: question

  A->>M: HTTPS request with messages

blocks.caption: To the service it is a slow HTTP call: apply timeouts, retries with backoff, and rate limits.

rows: Stream responses; never hold a database transaction during the call
Test with evaluations rather than exact matches
Track usage per user; set limits; choose smaller models where they are enough
Retry with backoff, and design a fallback

blocks.code:
You are a support assistant for an online bookstore.

Answer using only the context below.
If the context does not contain the answer, say "I don't know" and suggest contacting support.
Reply in at most three sentences, and cite the document id, for example [doc-12].

<context>
{retrieved_documents}
</context>

<question>
{user_question}
</question>
blocks.title: Clear role, rules, delimited data, output format
Key points
blocks.text:
- LLMs are stateless, slow, costly and non-deterministic.
- Everything sent counts against the context window.
- Wrap calls with timeouts, retries, limits and logging.
- Separate instructions from untrusted data.

items.question: Why does a long chat get more expensive per message?
items.answer: The model is stateless, so the history is resent every time. Summarise or trim it.

items.question: Why not hold a database transaction open during an LLM call?
items.answer: The call can take many seconds, so it holds a connection and locks, and could exhaust the pool.

items.question: When would you use a low temperature?
items.answer: When you need consistency, such as extracting fields or classifying.
